newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - March 26.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - March 26.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sri Lankan press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

Palestinian President Yasser Arafat appeals to Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) rebels to return to the peace process. Arafat addressed the media in Colombo at the end of a two-day visit to Sri Lanka, his first.
Government considering changing current proportional representation (PR) system as it applies to local government elections.
Government considering local council elections in northern Jaffna district after its landslide victory in the poll held elsewhere in the country last week.
A high level Chinese cultural delegation headed by Vice Minister of Cultural Affairs to visit Sri Lanka form March 28 to 30.

LTTE declares three days of mourning in areas under their control to commemorate about 60 rebels killed in a clash with the navy on Sunday off the northeastern Mullaitivu coast. The Navy says more than 100 rebels were killed and 10 boats were destroyed in the attack.

State power monopoly Ceylon Electricity Board (CEB) has no plans for power cuts at least till after the Sinhala New Year in mid-April, board sources say. Many people expect power cuts after water levels in hydropower reservoirs dropped to dangerously low levels following a drought.

Police ordered to follow up on all election-related incidents reported to police stations. Independent monitoring groups say there was widespread vote rigging during poll and nearly 2,000 incidents of poll-related violence reported.
